neighbours.label: plump / fleshy fullness: 'ump' in plump (also trussed, fat)
fire: The market stall was piled with plump tomatoes and peppers.
A plump little robin hopped along the fence.
Soak the raisins until they are soft and plump.
The baby had plump cheeks and a wide smile.
She chose the plumpest chicken in the butcher's window.
Rain made the grapes swell and turn plump on the vine.
The cushions on the sofa looked plump and inviting.
He bit into a plump, juicy dumpling.
quiet: The market stall was piled with fresh tomatoes and peppers.
A small brown robin hopped along the fence.
Soak the raisins until they are soft and sweet.
The baby had rosy cheeks and a wide smile.
She chose the cheapest chicken in the butcher's window.
Rain made the grapes swell and ripen on the vine.
The cushions on the sofa looked soft and inviting.
He bit into a hot, juicy dumpling.
